reported.title: delete_document performs no admin or ownership check
reported.body: `delete_document` is exposed through `handle_delete_document`, which only resolves the caller's token. It never calls `_assert_admin` and never checks that the document belongs to the caller, so any authenticated user can delete any document in the table by guessing or enumerating `doc_id`. The audit log then records the deletion as legitimate. Add an authorization check (admin, or ownership via `get_document(doc_id, user)`) before executing the DELETE.

reported.title: purge_user swallows the admin check with except Exception: pass
reported.body: `_assert_admin` raises `Forbidden` for non-admins, but the call is wrapped in `try/except Exception: pass`, so the failure is discarded and execution continues to the DELETE statements. Any caller — admin or not — can delete every document owned by an arbitrary `target_user_id` plus the associated share rows. A check that fails silently is equivalent to no check at all.

reported.title: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded development value
reported.body: The signing key used by `auth.sign` (and therefore by share-link signatures in `sharing.py`) now defaults to the literal `"dev-secret-change-me"` when `QUORUM_DEMO_SECRET` is unset. A deployment that forgets the environment variable starts silently with a publicly known key, letting anyone forge valid signatures and share links. The previous fail-fast behaviour (`os.environ[...]`) made the misconfiguration impossible to miss.

reported.title: list_documents no longer clamps limit to MAX_PAGE_SIZE
reported.body: The clamp `min(int(limit), Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE)` was removed, so `handle_list_documents(token, limit=10**9)` now issues an unbounded query and materialises the whole result set as dicts in memory. Any authenticated caller can trigger this repeatedly to exhaust memory and saturate the database. If the export UI genuinely needs bigger pages, raise `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` rather than removing the ceiling.

reported.title: Export filename is joined unvalidated: path traversal outside export root
reported.body: `export_path` joins the caller-supplied `filename` onto the user's export directory with no validation. `filename = "../../etc/cron.d/job"` escapes the per-user directory, and an absolute path such as `"/etc/passwd"` makes `os.path.join` discard the base directory entirely, so `export_document` writes attacker-controlled JSON to any path the process can write. This is reachable from any authenticated user via `handle_export`. `reports.py` in this same PR sanitises through `validators.safe_export_name`; the same normalisation (or a `realpath` + `commonpath` containment check like `indexer.extract_text` does) is needed here.

reported.title: SQL injection: search term interpolated into query string
reported.body: `search()` builds SQL with an f-string, embedding the caller-supplied `term` (and `user["id"]`) directly into the statement. A term containing a single quote terminates the literal, e.g. `term = "x' OR 1=1 --"` breaks out of the MATCH literal, and `term = "x'; DROP TABLE documents; --"` (or a UNION SELECT to read other owners' rows) reaches the interpreter unescaped. This is reachable from any authenticated user via `handle_search`. The neighbouring `suggest()` shows the correct pattern: bind values as parameters. Only `column` is safe because it comes from the SORTABLE allowlist; `term` and the owner id must be passed as bound parameters.

reported.title: Mutable default argument leaks scopes between share links
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` is evaluated once at function definition, so the same list object is reused for every call that omits `scopes`. Line 20 appends `"read"` to it, and any caller that passes a list mutates their own argument too. After the first default-argument call the shared list already contains `"read"`; more importantly, `handle_create_share` passes user-supplied scope lists through, and repeated default-argument calls keep accumulating whatever was appended, so a later share link can be minted with scopes the requester never asked for. Use `scopes: list = None` and build a fresh copy inside the function (`scopes = list(scopes or [])`) before appending.

reported.title: TOCTOU between existence check and open() in export_document
reported.body: `export_document` checks `os.path.exists(destination)`, then sleeps 200 ms, then opens the path with mode `"w"`. Anything created at that path during the window — including by a concurrent export request from the same user or a symlink planted in the shared export root — is silently truncated and overwritten, defeating the `FileExistsError` guard. Use an atomic exclusive create instead: open with mode `"x"` (or `os.open` with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`) and catch `FileExistsError` from the open itself.

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme or host allowlist
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document` passes the caller's `url` straight to `requests.get` with redirects enabled by default. There is no validation of scheme or host, so a user can point the import at `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/` (cloud metadata), `http://127.0.0.1:.../` internal admin endpoints, or `file://`-adjacent handlers, and the response body is returned to them as the document `body`. Validate the parsed scheme against `{http, https}`, resolve the host and reject private/link-local/loopback addresses, and disable automatic redirects (or re-validate each hop).

reported.title: Share links never expire: TTL stored as a duration and never checked
reported.body: `expires_at` is just the TTL in seconds (`ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`) with no creation timestamp added, and it is written into the `expires_in` column. `resolve_share_link` selects only `doc_id, scopes` and never compares anything against the current time, so every share link is valid forever once minted. Store an absolute expiry (`time.time() + ttl`) and reject rows whose expiry is in the past in `resolve_share_link`.

reported.title: Share signature compared with != instead of a constant-time compare
reported.body: `resolve_share_link` validates the share MAC with a plain string comparison, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. An attacker who can submit many resolve attempts for a known `doc_id`/`token` can use the timing difference to recover a valid signature byte by byte. Compare with `hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)` (requires importing `hmac`).

reported.title: resolve_share_link ignores the scopes it just fetched
reported.body: The share row's `scopes` column is read into `share` and then discarded: the function returns the full document row (`SELECT * FROM documents`) regardless of whether the link was minted read-only or with a narrower scope. Any recipient of a share link therefore gets the complete record, defeating the scope narrowing that `create_share_link` advertises. The returned payload should be filtered according to `share["scopes"]`.

reported.title: list_documents no longer clamps limit to MAX_PAGE_SIZE

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme or host allowlist

reported.title: SQL injection in search() via f-string interpolation of term
reported.body: `term` (and the sort column and limit) are interpolated directly into the SQL string with an f-string. `handle_search` passes the caller-supplied term straight through, so a term containing a single quote breaks out of the literal, e.g. `x' OR 1=1 --` returns every row regardless of `owner_id`, and stacked/subquery payloads can read other users' documents. reported.title: Mutable default argument shared across create_share_link calls
reported.body: `scopes: list = []` is evaluated once at function definition, so every call that omits `scopes` shares the same list object, which the body then mutates via `scopes.append("read")`. The same object is also returned to the caller in the result dict; any mutation of that returned list (or of the default by any other path) leaks into the scopes granted by all subsequent share links, silently widening permissions on links minted later.

reported.title: Share signature compared with != instead of constant-time compare
reported.body: `resolve_share_link` compares the recomputed HMAC/signature with the attacker-supplied one using `!=`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. An attacker who can time repeated `resolve_share_link` calls for a chosen `doc_id`/`token` can recover a valid signature byte by byte. Use `secrets.compare_digest`, which is already importable here.

reported.title: SSRF: user-supplied URL fetched with no scheme or host allowlist
reported.body: `fetch_remote_document` issues `requests.get` against a URL taken verbatim from the caller (`handle_import_url`). There is no scheme restriction and no host allowlist, so an authenticated user can point the import at internal addresses — `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/` on EC2, `http://metadata.google.internal/...` on GCP, `http://127.0.0.1:*/` for internal admin ports, or `file://` — and the response body is returned to them in the `body` field. Redirects are also followed by default, so an allowlist would need `allow_redirects=False` or per-hop validation. Validate the parsed scheme against `{"http","https"}` and resolve the host, rejecting loopback/link-local/private ranges before the request.

reported.title: Share links never expire: TTL stored as a duration and never checked
reported.body: `expires_at` is set to the raw TTL in seconds (`ttl or DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`), not an absolute timestamp, and is written into the `expires_in` column. `resolve_share_link` selects only `doc_id, scopes` and never compares anything against the current time, so a share link remains valid forever. Any leaked share token plus signature grants permanent access to the document. Store `time.time() + ttl` and reject rows whose expiry has passed in `resolve_share_link`.

reported.title: resolve_share_link ignores share scopes and returns the whole row
reported.body: After validating the link, the function looks up the document with `SELECT *` and returns every column, discarding the `scopes` value it just fetched. A share minted as read-only therefore hands the recipient the full document record, including any columns the owner did not intend to expose, and no caller can enforce the scope because it is not returned. Return the scopes alongside the document (or filter the columns) so the scope restriction is actually applied.

reported.title: TOCTOU between existence check and write, widened by a 0.2s sleep
reported.body: `export_document` checks `os.path.exists(destination)`, then sleeps 200 ms, then opens the path with mode `"w"`. Two concurrent exports of the same filename both pass the check and the second silently truncates and overwrites the first — the `FileExistsError` guard is unenforceable. The deliberate `time.sleep(0.2)` makes the race window large enough to hit routinely. Open with `os.open(destination, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)` (wrapped in `os.fdopen`) so the create-if-absent is atomic, and drop the sleep.

survived.title: SQL injection: search term interpolated into query string
survived.body: `search()` builds its SQL with an f-string, embedding the caller-supplied `term` directly inside a single-quoted SQL literal and `user["id"]` unquoted. Any request reaching `handle_search(token, term)` with a term containing a single quote breaks out of the literal, e.g. `term = "x' OR 1=1 --"` drops the `owner_id` restriction and returns other users' documents; a term containing `'; DROP TABLE documents; --` or a subselect can read or alter arbitrary tables depending on the driver. `suggest()` in the same module shows the correct parameterised form, so `db.query` supports bound parameters.

survived.title: Admin check in purge_user swallowed by bare except
survived.body: `_assert_admin` raises `Forbidden` for non-admins, but the call is wrapped in `try/except Exception: pass`, so the failure is discarded and execution continues to the destructive `DELETE`. Any authenticated non-admin who reaches `purge_user` can wipe every document belonging to an arbitrary `target_user_id`, plus the associated share rows. A check that fails silently is equivalent to no check.

survived.title: delete_document performs no authorization check
survived.body: `delete_document` deletes any row by primary key with no admin check and no owner check, yet it is exposed to every authenticated caller through `handle_delete_document` in `app/__init__.py`. Any logged-in user can pass an arbitrary `doc_id` and permanently destroy another user's document. The module already defines `_assert_admin`, and `documents.get_document` performs the owner check, but neither is invoked here.

survived.title: Path traversal: export filename joined without sanitisation
survived.body: `export_path` joins the caller-supplied `filename` straight onto the user's export directory. `handle_export(token, doc_id, filename)` passes it through unchecked, so a filename of `../../etc/cron.d/job` or `../<other_user_id>/notes.json` escapes the per-user directory and writes attacker-controlled JSON anywhere the process can write. `reports.write_report` in this same PR runs the filename through `validators.safe_export_name` first; `export.py` does not. Fix by importing `validators` and wrapping the filename (`os.path.join(user_dir, validators.safe_export_name(filename))`), or by resolving with `os.path.realpath` and rejecting anything outside `user_dir` as `indexer.extract_text` does.

survived.title: Mutable default argument leaks scopes between share links
survived.body: `scopes: list = []` binds a single list object at function definition time, and the body mutates it via `scopes.append("read")`. Every call that omits `scopes` shares that one list. Worse, a caller who passes a list has it mutated in place. Over the process lifetime the default list accumulates entries — and because `handle_create_share` forwards caller-supplied scopes, a scope granted on one share can be persisted into the default and then silently attached to a later share created by a different user, widening what a share recipient may do.

survived.title: list_documents no longer clamps limit to MAX_PAGE_SIZE
survived.body: The `min(..., Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE)` clamp was removed, so `handle_list_documents(token, limit=...)` passes an unbounded caller-controlled value into the query. Any authenticated user can request `limit=100000000` and force the whole table to be materialised into a list of dicts in memory, exhausting memory and stalling the process — a trivially reachable denial of service. `Config.MAX_PAGE_SIZE` is now unused.

survived.title: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded development value
survived.body: `SECRET_KEY` now defaults to the literal `"dev-secret-change-me"` when `QUORUM_DEMO_SECRET` is unset. This key is used by `auth.sign` to sign share links (`sharing.create_share_link` / `resolve_share_link`); a deployment that forgets the environment variable silently runs with a publicly known key, allowing anyone to forge a valid share signature for any `doc_id` and read documents they do not own. The previous fail-fast `os.environ[...]` lookup made a misconfiguration impossible to ship.
